passage:
Ken found a shortcut to school through a small alley. It looked faster on the map, so he tried it.
At first, it saved time. But after a week, road work began in the alley. He had to walk around machines, mud, and parked scooters. Sometimes he arrived later than before.
His sister laughed and called it "the long shortcut."
Ken went back to his old route. It was not the shortest on the map, but it was clear, safe, and easy to walk.
He learned that faster is not always better. A good route is not only about distance. It is also about what happens along the way.
